problem: Existing LSTM-based speaker models used for back-translation data augmentation in VLN cannot exploit long-range spatio-temporal dependencies across panoramas and steps, and they misalign generated instructions with trajectories (missing or repeated actions), producing noisy pseudo-labels. Transformer speakers also overfit on the small R2R data.
motivation: Speaker quality directly determines the quality of pseudo-instructions and thus follower generalization, yet it has been largely overlooked. A poor speaker adds noise and wrong supervision. Humans segment a path into stages and describe each, which suggests giving the speaker a notion of progress.
key_idea: A transformer speaker with a spatial (action-query cross-attention over the panorama) plus temporal encoder, an auxiliary speaker progress monitor regressing per-word progress from FGR2R sub-instruction segmentation, and five-position multifeature dropout to curb overfitting.
insight: Multihead cross-attention fusion of action and panorama beats soft attention, and adding BLSTM on top gives no gain (ablation table). SPM helps only when the auxiliary weight is smaller than the main loss (lambda=0.8 best, 0.4 hurts). Extending dropout from MFD1-3 to MFD1-5 improves all unseen metrics (SPICE 20.3 to 21.5), and each PASTS component (ST, SPM, MFD) incrementally improves HAMT's unseen SR/SPL, so a better speaker yields a better follower.
method: Spatial encoder: multihead cross-modal attention with the action-level (oriented) image feature as query and the 36-view panorama features as key/value, with residual and LayerNorm, giving one fused token per step
Temporal encoder: 6-layer transformer encoder over the step tokens with position embeddings to model inter-step dependencies
Text decoder: 6-layer autoregressive transformer decoder with masked attention and a speaker word projector (SWP) trained with cross-entropy

Speaker Progress Monitor (SPM): parallel MLP head on the decoder's last hidden layer regressing each word's progress j/K (from FGR2R sub-instruction segmentation) with MSE; joint loss lambda*L_SWP+(1-lambda)*omega*L_SPM, lambda=0.8, omega=10
Multifeature dropout (MFD): five dropouts (environment dropout on input features 0.3, FFN activation, attention matrix, QKV, and output projection, each 0.2)

Back translation: trained PASTS labels the 665k PREVALENT-sampled trajectories with environment dropout, and the follower is trained alternating original and augmented data (EnvDrop, RecBERT, HAMT, DUET)

setting.backbone: PASTS speaker: 6-layer spatio-temporal transformer encoder plus 6-layer decoder, trained from scratch on ResNet-152/ViT-B/16/CLIP-B/32 features; followers EnvDrop, RecBERT, HAMT, DUET
setting.training_data: R2R train instructions plus FGR2R sub-path/sub-instruction segmentation for SPM; back translation over 665,206 PREVALENT-sampled trajectories with pseudo-instructions for follower training
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views per viewpoint with orientation features)
setting.privileged: none at test time (FGR2R segmentation only used for speaker training)

numbers.backbone: DUET with ViT-B/16 features, PASTS back translation
numbers.extra: augmented with PREVALENT trajectories labeled by PASTS
back translation with PASTS; single-run test

numbers_note: Also reports speaker caption metrics (val-unseen, ViT-B/16 PASTS: BLEU-1 57.9, BLEU-4 18.5, ROUGE-L 37.0, CIDEr 16.8, SPICE 22.9), not included as navigation numbers. Table 4 HAMT+PASTS full: val-unseen SR 68.28 / SPL 62.37, val-seen SR 77.47 / SPL 73.54. Navigation results are printed as integers.
results: PASTS beats prior speakers (Speaker-Follower, WIP, Env, Cmp, Imp-Speaker) on all speaker metrics under ResNet-152 features (val-unseen BLEU-4 17.6, SPICE 21.5). As augmentation it improves four followers, e.g. EnvDrop val-unseen SR 52 to 55, HAMT 66 to 68, and DUET test SR 69 to 70 / SPL 59 to 60, with DUET+PASTS reaching state-of-the-art on R2R.
limitations: Generated instructions are shorter and contain fewer object words than human ones, since only image features are used, with no object-level representation
Gains on strong pretrained followers are small (e.g. DUET val-unseen SR unchanged at 72), and a few metrics degrade (RecBERT val-seen)
Depends on FGR2R sub-instruction annotations for the progress supervision
